parsed_artifact.adjudicated_statement: Work over C with Q-coefficients at (g,n)=(6,6). Let T:=W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q), identified by Poincare duality with W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21) (FND-0001). For any closed substack Y' of the smooth Deligne-Mumford stack M_{6,6}, write K(Y'):=ker(T->W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6} minus Y';Q)(21)) for the associated kernel-form term. Poincare-Verdier duality on the smooth ambient identifies K(Y') with the image of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y';Q)->T (FND-0180, FND-0168(3a)), without a closed embedding of a Casnati-Ekedahl model, a regular immersion or lci hypothesis, a Gysin shift, or a map from the cohomology of Z. If W is a separated finite-type C-scheme of dimension delta, then H_c^k(W;Q)=0 and H^{BM}_k(W;Q)=0 for all k>2 delta; equivalently, an n-dimensional complex scheme has vanishing Borel-Moore homology in all degrees strictly greater than 2n. With Q-coefficients the same vanishing passes to a closed Deligne-Mumford substack admitting a finite-type scheme atlas of dimension delta, and also to Borel-Moore homology of Y' as defined by cohomology with supports along Y' in the smooth ambient. Consequently, if dim Y'<8 then H^{BM}_{16}(Y';Q)=0 and K(Y')=0. Nested-open factorization of ordinary restriction (if Y' subset Y then the complement of Y is contained in the complement of Y') yields K(Y') subset T_Z for the ATT-0120 support Y, without requiring Y' to contain the full Casnati-Ekedahl classifying image. Therefore a closed substack can inject a nonzero subspace into this named T_Z only if it has dimension at least 8. Combined with the corroborated bound dim Y<=20 (FND-0181), any such contributing closed substack of Y lies in the range 8<=dim<=20; the sharper bound dim Y<=17 is not used and remains unproved. In particular, for any constant or product clause-(E) model Z_B=B x Z_0, the classifying morphism to M_{6,6} factors through the fibrewise ordered reduced-support open Z_0 in a single Abel-Jacobi P^2 on a single fixed curve, so the geometric image has dimension at most 2 and the reduced closure Y_0 satisfies dim Y_0<=2<8; hence K(Y_0)=0 and the model contributes the zero subspace of T_Z. Such models are inert in both directions relative to the exact C66-TATE-SUPPORT theorem: they can neither exhibit a non-Tate subquotient of this named T_Z nor supply a nonzero Tate summand of T_Z, whatever their standalone Hodge types, including the FND-0178 type-(10,6) class. This exclusion uses only support-side vanishing of the kernel-form term. It does not use, and does not require, a compact-support pushforward along the non-proper classifying morphism.
parsed_artifact.contradiction_resolution: No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty, and the candidate does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001 through THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. Mandatory first reads of ATT-0121 and REV-0171 confirm the contested passages. ATT-0121 Section 4 asserts ordinary vanishing H_c^k(W;Q)=0 for k>2 dim W on separated finite-type C-schemes, hence H_c^{16}=H^{BM}_{16}=0 once dim<8, and concludes that a closed substack of M_{6,6} with a finite-type scheme atlas of dimension less than 8 contributes the zero kernel-form subspace to T_Z. REV-0171 independently confirmed this as CLM-0121-3, including Q-coefficient passage from a scheme atlas to a closed Deligne-Mumford substack and exactness of W_{-16} on the Borel-Moore localization sequence matching FND-0168(3a) and FND-0180, with no Gysin or regularity hypothesis. ATT-0121 Section 5 and CLM-0121-4 additionally claim that compact-support pushforward along a constant clause-(E) classifying morphism factors as f_{B,!}=f_{0,!} o pr_! and vanishes on H_c^{16}(Z_B). REV-0171 correctly marks that claim unresolved: a classifying morphism Z->M_{6,6} is not proper, so there is no map H_c^{16}(Z)->H_c^{16}(M_{6,6}), matching FND-0180's recorded absence of a map from the cohomology of Z to T. The support-side conclusion of Section 5 is nevertheless independently verified: the constant type-(i) classifying image lies in the at-most-two-dimensional set of ordered reduced members of a single linear system on a single fixed curve, so the reduced closure Y_0 has dim<=2 and W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y_0;Q)=0. The candidate already states that exclusion needs no compact-support pushforward; the audit retains that correction and discards the f_! language. CLM-0121-2 (dim Y<=17 from an Hbar^bal atlas plus CLM-0112-8) is unresolved in REV-0171 because ATT-0112/CLM-0112-8 is confirmed only over smooth finite-type atlases of H^bal, not etale atlases of Hbar^bal. FND-0181 only corroborates dim Y<=20 and explicitly does not assert equality dim Y=17. The original candidate's range 8<=dim<=17 is therefore not packet-ready; the dimension floor 8 is independent of that upper bound. FND-0182 monotonicity is stated only for nested closed substacks both containing the full CE classifying image Im; the needed containment of a smaller kernel-form term inside T_Z follows instead from nested-open factorization of ordinary restriction (if Y' subset Y then U_Y subset U_{Y'}, so ker(Y') subset ker(Y)=T_Z) and does not require Im subset |Y'|. Distinct from FND-0181 (properness of Y, dim Y<=20), FND-0182 (monotonicity for supports containing Im), FND-0178 (standalone type-(10,6) class with an explicit disclaimer of any M_{6,6} image), and FND-0165 (scheme-level compact-support localization, which withholds a standalone stack compact-support MHS). Compatible with FND-0180: T_Z is the image of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q)->T via Poincare-Verdier on the smooth ambient, so vanishing of H^{BM}_{16}(Y') forces the kernel-form term of Y' to vanish without identifying T_Z with the supports group. Live primary sources agree: Can arXiv:1903.06849v1, following Fulton Intersection Theory Ch. 19, records that an n-dimensional complex scheme has Borel-Moore homology zero in all degrees >2n, with H^{BM}_{2n} free on irreducible components; Wikipedia oldid 1363651720 records that over Z one has the UCT 0->Ext(H_c^{i+1},Z)->H_i^{BM}->Hom(H_c^i,Z)->0, hence over Q one has H_i^{BM}(X;Q) isomorphic to Hom(H_c^i(X;Q),Q) with no extra Tate twist (matching FND-0165), that BM homology is covariant only for proper maps, and that H_k^{BM}(R^n) is Z in degree n and otherwise zero; Deligne, Theorie de Hodge III, Theorem 8.2.4 (Publ. Math. IHES 44 (1974), p. 38 of the IAS PDF) forces Hodge numbers of H^n(X) to vanish unless (p,q) lies in [n-N,N]x[n-N,N] when dim X=N, which is empty for n>2N and therefore yields vanishing of the group itself above twice the dimension. The screening rule is therefore a standard vanishing theorem applied to the corroborated kernel-form interface, not an attempt-specific gap. Promote the narrowed statement; do not merge.
